cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 1] Carus buys 500 measures of red wine from Daphne. In Daphne's cellar — in her presence and with her consent — he seals five barrels of 100 measures each and declares: “This wine now belongs to me.” Does Carus acquire possession?
cards.back:
Yes — Carus acquires possession of the five barrels (wine) with his declaration, derivatively by TRADITIO.
• The sale (EMPTIO VENDITIO) alone gives no possession; intention to buy ≠ ANIMUS POSSIDENDI.
• CORPUS unproblematic: Carus is in the cellar at the barrels and touches them.
• ANIMUS: according to Labeo/Ulpian, mere sealing does not suffice (D 18.6.1.2, Case 11 — only protection against substitution; Trebatius differs). Here, however, Carus expresses his possessory intent EXPRESSLY (“now belongs to me”) — ANIMUS can be declared expressly.
• Daphne consents in the presence of the goods → agreement on immediate transfer of possession → acquisition OCULIS ET AFFECTU (Paulus D 41.2.1.21, Case 4).
• If Daphne is the owner, Carus also acquires ownership with the sale as IUSTA CAUSA (wine = RES NEC MANCIPI).
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 1] Carus kauft von Daphne 500 Maßeinheiten Rotwein. In Daphnes Keller versiegelt er — in ihrer Anwesenheit und mit ihrer Zustimmung — fünf Fässer zu je 100 Maßeinheiten und erklärt: „Dieser Wein gehört jetzt mir.“ Erwirbt Carus Besitz?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 2] Helene has the art dealer Stilo show her silver statues, decides to buy a statue and declares that she wants to take it with her immediately; Stilo agrees. Shortly afterwards she asks Stilo to keep the statue for her until she comes back; three days later she collects it. When does Helene acquire possession?
cards.back:
Immediately with the agreement in the presence of the statue — OCULIS ET AFFECTU, not only on collection.
• Sale alone = no possession. Her declaration that she wants to take the statue with her immediately is express ANIMUS POSSIDENDI; Stilo's consent = agreement on immediate transfer of possession in the presence of the thing (Paulus D 41.2.1.21, Case 4). No seizing needed (not CORPORE ET TACTU).
• Through the request for safekeeping Stilo becomes her detentor (depositary, ANIMUS REM ALTERI HABENDI): immediate natural possession; Helene has mediate proprietary possession.
• (Had she not yet had possession, the safekeeping arrangement would have operated as CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM.)
• Collection after three days: Helene becomes immediate possessor, the detention ends; nothing changes as to who is possessor.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 2] Helene lässt sich beim Kunsthändler Stilo Silberstatuen zeigen, entschließt sich zum Kauf einer Statue und erklärt, sie sofort mitnehmen zu wollen; Stilo stimmt zu. Kurz darauf bittet sie Stilo, die Statue für sie aufzubewahren, bis sie wiederkommt; drei Tage später holt sie sie ab. Wann erwirbt Helene Besitz?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 3a] Quartus has bought goods from Ismene that are stored together with other things in a large warehouse. In front of the warehouse Ismene hands him the keys and leaves. The next day Quartus collects the goods. Has Quartus acquired possession? When?
cards.back:
Yes — already with the handover of the keys in front of the warehouse, not only on collection.
• Papinian D 18.1.74 (Case 5): whoever buys goods stored in a warehouse acquires possession with the handover of the keys, provided it takes place at the warehouse.
• Cf Paulus D 41.2.1.21 (Case 4, case 4: cellar keys) — acquisition OCULIS ET AFFECTU; the key provides the possibility of access (CORPUS).
• ANIMUS: acceptance of the keys in the context of the sale.
• Problem: the goods lie together with others in a large warehouse — large, inaccessible stocks of goods make CORPUS more difficult; decisive is that the key provides access.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 3a] Quartus hat von Ismene Waren gekauft, die neben anderen Sachen in einem großen Magazin lagern. Vor dem Magazin übergibt Ismene ihm die Schlüssel und geht. Am nächsten Tag holt Quartus die Waren. Hat Quartus Besitz erworben? Wann?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 3b] Variant: in front of the warehouse Ismene hands Quartus the keys to the purchased goods; the next day Quartus finds that the keys do not lock. Has Quartus acquired possession?
cards.back:
No — the keys provide no access, hence no control (no CORPUS).
• The key establishes CORPUS only as a means of access (Gaius D 41.1.9.6, Case 6: if the store is locked and the keys are the only means of access; Papinian D 18.1.74).
• There is no possession through symbols (no TRADITIO FICTA).
• Ismene remains possessor.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 3b] Variante: Ismene übergibt Quartus vor dem Magazin die Schlüssel zu den gekauften Waren; am nächsten Tag stellt Quartus fest, dass die Schlüssel nicht sperren. Hat Quartus Besitz erworben?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 4] Ramses allows Juno to borrow his horse for two days. At night Tiro steals the horse from Juno, takes it to the market, sells it and delivers it to Vibia. What are the possessory relations in the course of the case?
cards.back:
1. At first: Ramses is (immediate) proprietary possessor.
2. Loan: Juno becomes detentor (ANIMUS REM ALTERI HABENDI) → immediate natural possession; Ramses retains mediate proprietary possession through Juno.
3. Theft: Tiro commits FURTUM and acquires ORIGINAL possession (ANIMUS REM SIBI HABENDI + CORPUS by his own act). Ramses' possession and Juno's detention end (cf Example 1: Hector).
4. Sale and delivery: Vibia acquires DERIVATIVE possession (TRADITIO); her possession rests on an IUSTA CAUSA (sale) → civil possession.
• Ownership remains with Ramses: Tiro could not transfer any; usucaption by Vibia is excluded (RES FURTIVA). Ramses: REI VINDICATIO against Vibia; against Tiro ACTIO FURTI + CONDICTIO FURTIVA.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 4] Ramses gestattet Juno, sein Pferd für zwei Tage auszuleihen. Nachts stiehlt Tiro das Pferd bei Juno, bringt es auf den Markt, verkauft und übergibt es an Vibia. Wie sind die Besitzverhältnisse im Laufe des Falls?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 5a] Felix asks his adult son-in-power Gripus to buy a flute player at the slave market. Gripus chooses a flautist and in addition a harpist; the dealer Hermes sells and delivers both to Gripus. Gripus brings them to his father, who is highly pleased. Who has possession at the individual stages?
cards.back:
Gripus is ALIENI IURIS → he cannot possess in his own name, but can acquire for Felix (ANIMO NOSTRO, CORPORE ALIENO).
• Flautist: Felix's ANIMUS lies in the IUSSUM for this transaction → Felix acquires possession already with the delivery from Hermes to Gripus.
• Harpist: no IUSSUM (and no PECULIUM) → with the delivery Felix does not yet acquire. His satisfaction is a RATIHABITIO → to be treated as if he had given a IUSSUM beforehand (Ulpian D 46.3.12.4). At the latest when Gripus brings him the slave, Felix has ANIMUS and CORPUS anyway.
• Gripus' own intention is irrelevant; only his INTELLECTUS POSSIDENDI is needed (given in an adult).
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 5a] Felix ersucht seinen erwachsenen Haussohn Gripus, auf dem Sklavenmarkt einen Flötenspieler zu kaufen. Gripus wählt einen Flötisten und zusätzlich einen Harfenisten; Händler Hermes verkauft und übergibt beide an Gripus. Gripus bringt sie dem Vater, der höchst zufrieden ist. Wer hat in den einzelnen Stadien Besitz?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 5b] At Felix's request his son-in-power Gripus buys a flautist and, on his own initiative, also a harpist; Hermes delivers both. What difference does it make if Gripus has a PECULIUM?
cards.back:
Felix acquires possession of BOTH slaves already with the delivery to Gripus — no RATIHABITIO is needed.
• Through the PECULIUM the DOMINUS expresses his possessory intent in general, abstract terms; whatever the holder acquires, he acquires for him.
• The authorisation covers all transactions of the PECULIUM holder, not only those typical of the branch; Gripus concretises the ANIMUS (ANIMO SERVORUM).
• Felix need not even know of the acquisition (Paulus D 41.2.1.5, Case 25).
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 5b] Felix' Haussohn Gripus kauft auf Felix' Bitte einen Flötisten und eigenmächtig zusätzlich einen Harfenisten; Hermes übergibt beide. Welcher Unterschied ergibt sich, wenn Gripus ein PECULIUM hat?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 5c] At the request of his father Felix, Gripus buys a flautist and, on his own initiative, a harpist; Hermes delivers both to Gripus, Gripus brings them to his father. What is the position as to possession if Gripus is emancipated (free of power, SUI IURIS)?
cards.back:
Gripus himself acquires possession of both slaves (in his own name); Felix acquires only when Gripus delivers them to him (derivatively, TRADITIO).
• In pre-classical and classical law, persons free of power cannot acquire possession directly for others (Gai Inst 2.95; Paul Sent 5.2.2) → only indirect agency (cf Example 11, Primus/Secunda).
• Gripus is neither TUTOR, CURATOR nor PROCURATOR → no exception.
• Only under Justinian would direct agency be possible.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 5c] Gripus kauft auf Bitte seines Vaters Felix einen Flötisten und eigenmächtig einen Harfenisten; Hermes übergibt beide an Gripus, Gripus bringt sie dem Vater. Wie ist die Besitzlage, wenn Gripus emanzipiert (gewaltfrei, SUI IURIS) ist?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 6] At his request, Daphne lets her nephew Eros use her cart. On his birthday she declares: “I give you the cart, you can keep it.” Eros agrees. What are the possessory positions in the course of events?
cards.back:
1. Grant of use (loan or PRECARIUM): Eros becomes detentor (ANIMUS REM ALTERI HABENDI) → immediate natural possession; Daphne retains mediate proprietary possession.
2. Donation: TRADITIO BREVI MANU — Daphne gives up her ANIMUS REM SIBI HABENDI, and with her consent Eros henceforth holds the cart in his own name; he already has CORPUS (cf Gaius D 41.1.9.5, Case 12).
• Eros becomes proprietary possessor; if Daphne is the owner, he also becomes owner with the donation as IUSTA CAUSA.
• No violation of NEMO SIBI IPSE CAUSAM POSSESSIONIS MUTARE POTEST, because both parties agree.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 6] Daphne überlässt ihrem Neffen Eros auf dessen Bitte ihren Wagen zum Gebrauch. Zu seinem Geburtstag erklärt sie: „Ich schenke dir den Wagen, du kannst ihn behalten.“ Eros ist einverstanden. Wie sind die Besitzpositionen im Verlauf?

cards.topic: 13.10. Possession I — Case sheet unit 1 (Dr. Binder)
cards.front: [Case sheet 13.10. · Case 7] Nike sells and delivers (TRADITIO) a draught ox to Orion. Orion gives it to his slave Ramses, who runs a farm of Orion's in the neighbouring village. Later Pius convinces Orion that the ox belongs to him; Orion asks Pius to let him have the ox on lease for the harvest, and Pius agrees. Who possesses at the individual stages?
cards.back:
1. TRADITIO by Nike: Orion acquires possession derivatively.
2. Handover to the slave Ramses: Ramses is a possessor's agent (ALIENI IURIS), not a detentor → Orion retains IMMEDIATE possession through his “extended arm”.
3. Lease from Pius: Orion acknowledges Pius' possessory intent and henceforth holds the ox for him → Orion becomes detentor (lessee, natural possession; CORPUS continues to be exercised by his slave), Pius acquires MEDIATE proprietary possession.
• As in Iavolenus D 41.2.21.3 (Case 19); the process can be interpreted as CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM.
• No violation of NEMO SIBI IPSE …, because both agree. Whether Pius really is the owner is irrelevant for possession.
cards.old_front: [Fallblatt 13.10. · Fall 7] Nike verkauft und tradiert einen Zugochsen an Orion. Orion gibt ihn seinem Sklaven Ramses, der im Nachbardorf ein Gehöft des Orion bewirtschaftet. Später überzeugt Pius den Orion, dass der Ochse ihm gehöre; Orion bittet Pius, ihm den Ochsen für die Ernte mietweise zu überlassen, Pius ist einverstanden. Wer besitzt in den einzelnen Stadien?
